title: An atmospheric vacuum breaker is simple—and limited to the right pressure pattern
description: Identify an AVB, understand its atmospheric vent, and separate non-continuous use from PVB and hose-connection devices.
prompt: Does the device stay under pressure?
answer: An AVB prevents backsiphonage by opening to atmosphere. It is generally selected for non-continuous pressure and is not a substitute for a testable PVB where backpressure or continuous pressure exists.
urgency: Do not place a downstream shutoff where it leaves an AVB continuously pressurized unless the exact approved design and local rule allow it.
diagramAlt: Atmospheric vacuum breaker highlighting the air inlet and downstream valve restriction
identifiers: No field test cocks on a basic AVB.
An atmospheric opening admits air when supply pressure falls.
